<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/service-storage`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **75** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-access-hooks.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**53** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 157051ceb48d2d9ed289f21f7018a39ce7249178`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-access-hooks.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **15** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 157051ceb48d2d9ed289f21f7018a39ce7249178` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a0a0df0ca297c424c0cca9dd6594d7907ada705d` — the merge of head `3ec4b7b3ffc08a3ef131b6121e7fb6109f63f7a4` into base `157051ceb48d2d9ed289f21f7018a39ce7249178`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a0a0df0ca297c424c0cca9dd6594d7907ada705d && git checkout a0a0df0ca297c424c0cca9dd6594d7907ada705d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 157051ceb48d2d9ed289f21f7018a39ce7249178 3ec4b7b3ffc08a3ef131b6121e7fb6109f63f7a4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 157051ceb48d2d9ed289f21f7018a39ce7249178 && git merge --no-ff 3ec4b7b3ffc08a3ef131b6121e7fb6109f63f7a4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 157051ceb48d2d9ed289f21f7018a39ce7249178
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 157051ceb48d2d9ed289f21f7018a39ce7249178` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e1387f66c4beb4063d663367af722e0a36cf8482`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/platform-baseline-sets.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-security-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-member-grant.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-service-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-access-hooks.ts

Faces: schema and declaration, one record. Read: card #32754 and its ten comments (ruling 6837170004, the review it adopted, analysis 6833029287, report 6839436462), the PR body, its file list, the net diff against merge-base `5fb79bc0`, and the head's check-runs. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed.

Check-runs at 2026-11-13T00:14Z: 53 success, 10 skipped, 4 still running (three Test Core shards, Test UI), none failed. `Check Changeset`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` and the type checks are green. The landing check reads them again.

Result: one must-fix, two should-fix, five nits. The three conditions of the ruling are met as written; the must-fix is a fourth gate the ruling's rule covers and the head does not.

### ① Derived judgments

Public surface:

- `ISecurityService` gains one optional member, `contributePlatformBaselineSet`. Right: a widening. Absence is typed, and `security-service.test.ts` pins that an unguarded call does not compile.
- Two contract types are exported, `PlatformBaselineSetContribution` and `PlatformBaselineSetAdmission`. Right: `api-surface` and `export-origins` carry both. The contribution type admits read and create only, and the same test pins that an edit bit and a row policy do not compile.
- The registered `security` service serves the member. Right: the declared-members pin lists it as optional.
- Neither new module is re-exported from its package index. Right: no package surface moves beyond the spec member.
- No authorable key, manifest key or route reaches the seam. Right: `Metadata-protocol: none` holds.

Runtime accept-set:

- A member is admitted read and create on the attachment object where the object grant refused before. Right, and it is the ruling. Nothing else is granted: the set's body is pinned literally, and the seam admits by allow-list.
- The `everyone` definition names one more set, and explain attributes the grant to it as an additive baseline. Right: one distribution channel, as ADR-0090 D5 requires.
- A member who can read a record but not edit it now gets the attach rule's refusal code instead of the object grant's. The status stays 403. Right in code; the changeset does not say it (nit 1).
- An external member resolves its own baseline and gains nothing. Right, pinned on the real resolver.
- An agent principal's own leg gains nothing. Right. An agent acting for a member is bounded by that member, whom this change widens. The head's text says agents gain nothing (should-fix 1).
- A deployment that declares no member baseline admits the set and hands it to no one. Right, pinned.
- An object that has not opted in to attachments is refused where the opt-in gate is installed. Right there, pinned on the full stack. The head states the refusal without that condition (must-fix 1).

The ruling's conditions:

| Condition | Met | Pin |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Grant only with all three row gates | Yes. The read-visibility flag is the same expression that guards the install, and the call sits after the last gate. | `storage-service-plugin.test.ts`: no middleware seam, no auth service, no hook seam, each with no contribution and a warning naming the gate; plus the install order. `attachment-member-grant.test.ts`: each gate alone. Forcing any flag true turns its pin red. |
| 2. Own objects, read and create only, no wildcard, no elevated bit, no row policy, boot only | Yes. Keys and bits are allow-lists, so a bit set to false is refused too. The owner comes from the registry. The anchor predicate runs again on the parsed set. Every refusal precedes any write. | `platform-baseline-sets.test.ts`, one case per refusal. `platform-baseline-sets.integration.test.ts`: another package's object on the real registry, and the closed window on a booted kernel. |
| 2. Every contribution logged | Yes in code: info on admission, warn on refusal. | None (should-fix 2). |
| 2. ADR-0090 sentence in a separate PR | Yes: `docs/adr` is untouched. | n/a |
| 3. Changeset states the upgrade-day change | Yes. | Dogfood: another user's attachment on a readable record is listed and readable. |

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/plugin-security` and `@objectstack/service-storage`. Right: the three packages the diff moves, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch` (AGENTS.md step 3).
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is line-initial in the PR body and the changeset. Right: a published interface gains an optional member.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`. Right: no key, value or metadata type is added, and precedent #30108 read a baseline grant the same way. No third line is owed.
- Changeset prose: one overclaim (should-fix 1), one omission (nit 1), and one sentence that depends on must-fix 1.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation "contract review is the seat's": this record.
- Dev deviation "merged main once": confirmed. One merge commit, merge-base `5fb79bc0`.
- File surface: the report names 23 paths. They equal the diff and the PR's file list. The surface is wider than the claim's (plugin-security, spec, dogfood); the ruling allowed that and asked for exact paths, and they are named.
- No `open_questions` entry.
- The ADR-0090 sentence is owed as a separate Tier H PR. Until it lands, the contract docblock and the module doc are the only text saying the seam is for always-on platform services. The seat tracks it.
- Out of scope, per the ruling: an uploader withdrawing their own attachment.
- Escalated: must-fix 1 has two routes, and the second needs the maintainer's word.
- Public text (PR body, changeset, docs page, test names, log strings) stays at rule level. No steps.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no author note.
- One private note set is with the seat.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts` (hit). Holds against the ruling and ADR-0090. The set is the contributor's own, with one package as its holder, so D9's objection to a communal set does not apply. It joins the baseline that `everyone` is derived from, so it is not the second channel Alternatives 3 rejected. The docblock matches the implementation sentence by sentence, with one exception (should-fix 1). First consumer: the storage service.

`platform-baseline-sets.ts`, `security-plugin-security-service.ts`, `security-plugin.ts`. Agree with the contract. The window closes at `kernel:bootstrapped` on both kernels. A set that joins after the anchor's derivation began causes one more derivation, pinned by the `everyone` definition case. Every baseline reader holds the one array.

`attachment-member-grant.ts`, `storage-service-plugin.ts`. Agree with condition 1 as written. Every outcome other than a contribution leaves members refused.

`attachment-access-hooks.ts`. Comment only; now true.

Findings:

- **must-fix 1. The grant does not wait for every gate on the attachment insert.** Ruling B was chosen over a static line for one reason: the grant exists only where the gates are installed, and a host missing one is refused loudly. The head waits for the three row gates the storage service installs. The review the ruling adopted also lists the per-object attachment opt-in as unchanged, and the head repeats that without a condition (the grant module's docblock, the docs page). The gate behind that refusal is not one of the three. The head does not check for it, and no pin boots a composition without it. Two routes: the grant waits for that gate as it waits for the other three, names it in the warning when it is missing, and a pin covers it; or the maintainer accepts the exception in words and the changeset states it. Detail is with the seat.
- **should-fix 1. "Agents gain nothing" is wider than the code.** It holds for an agent principal's own leg. An agent acting for a member reaches what both its own ceiling and that member allow (ADR-0090 D10), and the card's measured caller is such an agent. The docs page says it correctly. Align the changeset, the PR body and the contract docblock. Pin a delegated agent: admitted where its member and its scope both allow, refused otherwise.
- **should-fix 2. The logging limb of condition 2 has no pin.** Removing the seam's admission line or its refusal line leaves every suite green. Assert both.
- nit 1. The changeset omits the refusal-code change for a member who reads a record but may not edit it. Prose face.
- nit 2. The storage side types the seam with a local shape, not a `Pick` of the published member. Same as the #21729 precedent; accepted deviation.
- nit 3. The window's close hangs on the context exposing `hook`. Both kernels do; accepted deviation.
- nit 4. The no-security outcome is said at debug only. It fails closed; accepted deviation.
- nit 5. A dogfood comment calls one attachment "stored before the member held any grant"; the fixture grants from boot. The assertion is right, the comment is not.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e8eb97dc32d46ca89884cfddbfc1d1cfb05b0dc8`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/platform-baseline-sets.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-security-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-member-grant.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-service-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-access-hooks.ts

Face: schema. Delta review over the FAIL record 6839888392 on `e1387f66`. The compare is one commit ahead, no rebase, 11 files; every hunk of it was read. Hunks the delta does not touch keep the round-1 judgment and were not re-derived. Read: card #32754 and its ten comments (ruling 6837170004, analysis 6833029287), the PR body, file list and net diff, the round-1 record, the head's check-runs. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed.

Check-runs at 2026-11-13T01:24Z: 27 success, 12 skipped, 30 in progress (all eight Test Core shards, Test UI, three type checks, Build Core, two lint groups), none failed. `Check Changeset`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` are green. No red check; the landing check reads the rest.

Result: one must-fix, one should-fix, two nits. The round-1 must-fix is closed as it was written. Closing it by the first route moved the problem: the fourth gate is not part of the stock composition, so the grant no longer reaches it.

### Prior findings

| Round-1 finding | At this head | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| must-fix 1: the grant does not wait for the per-object opt-in gate | Fixed as written (route 1). A fourth flag, `filesOptIn`, is required; a kernel without the audit service contributes nothing and the warning names the gate. | `attachment-member-grant.test.ts` (the missing-gate case), `storage-service-plugin.test.ts` (no audit service), dogfood: a host with storage and security and no audit service answers 403 with no storage set. See new must-fix 1 and should-fix 1 for what the route left. |
| should-fix 1: "agents gain nothing" wider than the code | Fixed. The changeset, PR body, contract docblock, both module docs and the docs page now say: nothing on the agent's own leg; an agent acting for a member reaches what the member and its scope both allow. | Dogfood pin on an OAuth token: admitted on a record the member edits, refused with the attach rule's code on a readable-only record. The scope limb is pinned by the tool list, not by a refused call (nit 1). |
| should-fix 2: the logging limb has no pin | Fixed. | `platform-baseline-sets.integration.test.ts`: the admission line with its meta, the refusal line at warn with the contributor, the no-baseline admission line. |
| nit 1: changeset omits the refusal-code change | Fixed in the changeset. | |
| nit 5: wrong dogfood comment | Fixed. | |
| nits 2 to 4 | Unchanged; accepted deviations in round 1. | |

### ① Derived judgments

Public surface: unchanged from round 1. The delta touches the contract file in its docblock only; `api-surface` and `export-origins` do not move.

Runtime accept-set, as the delta changes it:

- A kernel with the storage service and no audit service: round 1 handed members read and create; this head hands them nothing. Right as a closing of round-1 must-fix 1. Wrong as an outcome for the card: see must-fix 1.
- The showcase on its CLI-wired composition: the round-1 head named the storage set on the `everyone` definition; this head removes that expectation from `showcase-d7-default-profile.dogfood.test.ts`. That is the tree saying the grant does not land there. The PR body does not say it.
- A kernel where a service is registered under the audit name and the opt-in gate is not installed: the grant is contributed. Wrong: should-fix 1.
- A member who reads but cannot edit a record: the attach rule's code instead of the object grant's, still 403. Right, and now stated in the changeset.
- A delegated agent: admitted where its member and its scope both allow. Right, pinned.
- No new accept on another tenant's or another user's records, on a read-only record, or on a system object: the set's body, the seam's allow-lists and the three row gates are untouched by the delta.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on the same three packages. Right; the delta adds no package and no surface.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, line-initial in the PR body and the changeset. Right.
- Changeset prose: the headline and the upgrade-day paragraph say every signed-in member can attach to the records they may edit. On a composition that does not mount the audit capability that is false at this head, and the text does not name the capability. Ruling condition 3 asks the changeset to state the upgrade-day change; this part of it is not stated (must-fix 1).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no author note.
- The PR body says nothing is needed from the maintainer. That no longer holds: must-fix 1 changes a consequence the ruling was accepted on, and its routes need the maintainer's word. Escalated.
- Whether the hosted runtime (the card's measured surface) mounts the audit capability cannot be read from this review's inputs. The card's own acceptance depends on it. Open, for the seat to answer with evidence.
- The ADR-0090 sentence is still a separate Tier H PR; `docs/adr` is untouched.
- Out of scope, per the ruling: an uploader withdrawing their own attachment.
- Public text stays at rule level.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts` (hit). Docblock only in the delta; it now matches the implementation on agents. Holds against the ruling and ADR-0090 D10.

`platform-baseline-sets.ts`. Comment only; true.

`security-plugin-security-service.ts`, `security-plugin.ts`, `attachment-access-hooks.ts`. Not touched by the delta.

`attachment-member-grant.ts`, `storage-service-plugin.ts`. The grant now waits for four flags. The fourth is read as "a service is registered under the audit name".

Findings:

- **must-fix 1. The fourth gate is not on the always-on slate, so the fix no longer reaches the stock composition, and no public text says so.** The ruling accepted B on a stated consequence: only a hand-composed host without the storage service keeps the 403, and the factory composition is unaffected. That rested on storage being always-on. The opt-in gate is installed by the audit plugin, which `PLATFORM_ALWAYS_ON_CAPABILITIES` does not list and which mounts only on `requires`. The three example apps and the `create-objectstack` blank template do not require it, and two of them declare `enable.files` on their objects. On those compositions a member who edits a record is still refused the attach, with a boot warning. The removed showcase expectation is the head's own measurement of this. The changeset headline and the docs page state the grant without naming the capability. Routes, each the maintainer's to choose: the opt-in gate becomes present wherever the storage service is (this changes what an app without the audit capability may attach to today, so it is a ruling, not a lane fix); or the maintainer accepts in words that a deployment without the audit capability gets no grant, and the changeset, the docs page and the warning name the capability an operator adds. Either way the PR states, with evidence, that the hosted runtime mounts the gate, because that is the surface the card was measured on.
- **should-fix 1. The fourth flag reads a service name, not the gate.** The other three flags are facts about what this plugin just installed or bound. This one is true for any object registered under the audit name: the unit pin registers an empty object there and the grant is contributed. The audit plugin registers its service at init and installs the gate later, in a handler that can end without installing it. The published platform skill's plugin example registers a service under that same name. In each case the grant is handed out where the gate is absent, which is the rule round-1 must-fix 1 named. Bind the flag to the gate itself (the installer states it, and the storage side reads that statement), and pin a kernel that has the name and not the gate.
- nit 1. The delegated-agent pin shows the scope limb through the tool list. A refused call on the read-only token would pin the door, not the menu.
- nit 2. The warning dropped its remedy sentence and names no other. An operator reading it is not told which capability to add.
